U.A. Support Course.name: U.A. Support Course
U.A. Support Course.description:
🔧 You design, build and repair the gear and costumes heroes depend on, working out of Power Loader's Development Studio.

🏫 Class 1-F, 1-G or 1-H: morning lectures, long workshop hours, repair orders with deadlines and test runs that go wrong.
⚖️ No license. Quirk use is legal in supervised workshop work and testing and in self-defense. Gear the school has not approved stays off the street.
🤝 Power Loader, Mei Hatsume of 1-H, Hero Course students with broken gear and scouting support companies all know your work.
🔓 Learnable later: Hazard-Proof Mod, Overnight Build.

📈 Grants: Technique +1, Support Engineering +10, Fabrication +10, Costume Design +5
⚡ Starting technique: Quirk-Fit Tuning
🎒 Starts with: U.A. school uniform, Workshop coveralls, Support toolkit, U.A. student ID, ¥10,000, School bag, Casual clothes, U.A. gym uniform
U.A. Support Course.traitNarrativeEffects:
Legal status: adult first-year, Support Course, Class 1-F, 1-G or 1-H. No hero license: Quirk use legal in supervised workshop work, testing and self-defense. Support items are regulated: unapproved gear stays off the street.
Access: campus, Studio tools and test bays (Power Loader's sign-off), parts stock, costume requests to support companies.
Obligations: design, engineering and materials classes, safety rules, order deadlines, exams, cleanup after failed tests; Heights Alliance dorms from day one, curfew.
Who notices: Power Loader (course teacher, Development Studio head, tired of explosions); Mei Hatsume of 1-H (builds day and night, causes most of them); Hero students with broken gear; scouting support companies; Sports Festival crowds.
Standing pressures: training-damaged Hero gear on deadline; at the Sports Festival they compete with their own gear as companies watch; pre-exam upgrade rushes; Mei keeps the Studio one explosion from a safety review.
